title: The absolute value of an algebraic element from its minimal polynomial constant term
statement: Let $K\subseteq E$ be fields [def-weil-field] equipped with compatible nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute values. Assume $K$ is complete for $d(x,y)=|x-y|$ and $E/K$ is algebraic, meaning that every element is a root of a nonzero polynomial in $K[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. For $x\in E$, let $m_x\in K[T]$ be its monic minimal polynomial [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and put $n=\deg m_x\ge1$. Then $$|x|=|m_x(0)|^{1/n}.$$ The right side is a nonnegative real power; the assertion includes $x=0$.
